anne: hey team — quick follow-up from the prefix+kv contract unification pilot we ran this week. found a couple of surprising correctness surface areas we should decide on before wider rollout :wave:

anne: tl;dr: reads after a demote/evict can observe stale prefix state for ~200-500ms under cross-node handoffs. not a catastrophic loss but breaks some SLOs for streaming cursor workloads. logs + small repro in the canary cluster.

julia: ack. do we have a minimal repro and stack trace?

anne: yes — repro lives in the canary job logs, snippet below. looks like tombstone applied on node A, handoff token clears on B, but readpath sees old residency flag until KV lease epoch update lands.

anne: ```
// simplified trace
PUT prefix X -> node A (epoch 42)
EVICT prefix X -> tombstone written, lease bumped to 43
Handoff starts -> node B takes ownership but cache mark still shows A's residency for ~300ms
Read cursor -> hits cached presence -> returns items that should be demoted
```

miguel: hmm. is this due to eventual consistency on lease broadcasts or our async residency invalidation?

anne: both. the unified API removed a small sync point we had previously that forced a lease refresh on handoff. saving ~1 RPC per handoff but introducing this window.

sam: cost vs correctness tradeoff. can we narrow the window without the heavy sync? e.g., publish a fast invalidation message and prefer strong read-after-write for active cursors?

liz: for customers with streaming cursors (video transcripts, long-running chat) this window matters. maybe make the sync point opt-in via config: `prefetch.strict_handoff=true`? defaults to false to keep perf.

julia: I like opt-in. also add a metric/alert: `prefetch.handoff_inconsistent_reads` and an eval that runs the repro against staging every deploy.

anne: proposed plan:
1) revert the removed forced lease-refresh in the unified path (cheap fix) behind a feature-flag `kv.unified.strict_handoff`
2) add `prefetch.handoff_inconsistent_reads` counter and a tracing span around handoff + read paths
3) run 72h canary with flag ON for 10% of production traffic, run repros as scheduled job
4) if stable, keep flag default ON for Dedicated/private, default OFF for Hosted for two releases, then flip after opt-in telemetry 

sam: timeframe?

anne: patch ready. want to deploy tomorrow morning (UTC) to canary cluster. canary window 72h -> iter -> wider rollout next week if ok.

miguel: please add chaos tests for cross-node handoff (kill node A mid-handoff) — I can wire that into our chaos suite. also add a unit test for lease-epoch fence logic.

anne: will do. also adding a regression test that asserts read-after-evict returns empty for a pinned cursor by advancing epoch on both nodes.

liz: docs/SDK impact? will any customers need SDK changes?

anne: no surface change; only config flags and better telemetry. but we'll add a short note in the release notes and a one-pager for SEs describing the tradeoffs.

julia: opsbot, create a deploy ticket for the canary with the repro job attached and assign to anne + miguel + sam.

opsbot: Ticket created: RDW-ENG-9873 — "canary: prefix-kv contract strict_handoff deploy + repro". Assignees: anne, miguel, sam. Canary window: 72h. Link: https://tickets.internal/9873 :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks. one more question — eviction fairness: does reverting the sync add back any tail-latency? we need to quantify for the Hosted SLOs.

anne: microbench showed +0.8ms p99 on handoff-heavy traces. i'll append the perf delta to the ticket.

miguel: ok let's run the chaos test and canary. if we still see inconsistent reads with the flag on, escalate to design review (but fingers crossed).

liz: and I'll draft the SE one-pager. include the config example and recommended settings for streaming workloads.

anne: config example we plan to document:

anne: ```yaml
kv: 
  unified_contract: true
  unified: 
    strict_handoff: true  # forces lease-refresh on handoff to eliminate stale-read window
```

anne: thanks everyone — will post canary results in this thread and link the ticket with perf numbers. :eyes:

opsbot: Deploy scheduled: canary cluster at 2026-03-24T07:00:00Z (auto-rollback set to 6h).
